subheading: TREATMENT OF HYPERGLYCEMIA IN A CHILD

text:
TREATMENT OF HYPERGLYCEMIA IN A CHILD
- The concentration of dextrose in infusion should be reduced.
- Insulin 0.05 - 0.1 IU/kg/hour should be commenced if RBG remains above
10 mmol/L with glycosuria despite reduction of glucose concentration in
infusion.
- Treat the identified cause if possible.

Table 19.1: Flow table for management of hyperglycaemia

- Blood glucose > 180 mg/dL (>10 mmol/L) with glucometer then recheck

- Confirm with a whole blood measurement in the laboratory

- Assess infant for possible underlying cause and treat
  - Sepsis
  - Excess glucose intake
  - Other illnesses
  - Exogenous corticosteroids orinotropes

Calculate the GIR glucose rate; if > 12 mg/kg/min: Reduce GIR and rate of flow

- Target blood glucose 100 - 180 mg/dL (5.5 - 9.9 mmol/L)
- Starting dose of insulin infusion 0.05-0.1 U/kg/hr
- Avoid hypoglycaemia
- Initially glucose should be monitored every 30 min for first hour
- Hourly thereafter, once glucose stabilized measure 4hourly
- Do not flush insulin infusion
